name: Brand24
description: Brand24 tracks your brand across 25M+ social, news, blog, forum and review sources with AI sentiment, anomaly alerts and an AI assistant. The money is in reselling the monitoring: monthly client reports and crisis-watch retainers on a single cheap seat.
visits: Monitors 25M+ web, social, news, blog, forum, review and podcast sources; G2 4.6/5 (1,500+ reviews); used by small brands, PR teams and marketing agencies worldwide.
pricing_details: Verified from brand24.com/pricing (October 2026). No free plan; 14-day free trial on every tier. Individual: $249/mo monthly or $199/mo billed annually - 3 keywords, 2,000 mentions/mo, 1 user, updates every 12h, AI sentiment analysis. Team: $349/mo monthly or $299/mo annually - 7 keywords, 10,000 mentions/mo, unlimited users, hourly updates, chat support. Pro: $499/mo monthly or $399/mo annually - 12 keywords, 40,000 mentions/mo, realtime updates, priority support, Lightning Search, AI Events Detection, AI Brand Assistant, AI Insights and AI Topics for 2 projects each. Business: $699/mo monthly or $599/mo annually - 25 keywords, 100,000 mentions/mo, AI Insights for 5 projects, unlimited AI Topics, Advanced Reports, named Client Success Lead. Enterprise: from $1,499/mo billed annually, custom keyword and mention limits, AI Visibility module, dedicated consulting. Annual billing saves roughly $600-1,200/yr depending on tier. Historical context: third-party reviews from 2025 list Individual at $79-149/mo, so list prices have roughly doubled to tripled in two years - negotiate or take annual billing.
pros: Source coverage is genuinely wide for the price - 25M+ sources including TikTok, Twitch, Telegram, podcasts, review sites and newsletters, not just the big four social networks
The alerting layer is the part worth paying for: anomaly detection spikes your phone when mentions explode, which is the crisis-catching moment that justifies the bill
Unlimited users from the Team plan up, so an agency can put every account manager in one project without per-seat math
AI Insights and AI Topics (Pro and up) actually summarize conversation clusters instead of dumping raw mentions, which cuts report-building from hours to minutes
Cheaper than every enterprise alternative by an order of magnitude - Business at $699/mo does work that Brandwatch sells at $2,000-5,000/mo
cons: Prices have climbed hard: Individual went from $79 in older reviews to $249 monthly now, and the trajectory suggests more hikes - lock annual rates and expect renewal pain
Keyword caps are stingy - 3 keywords on Individual and 12 on Pro means a client with a brand, a founder name and two product lines already eats the whole quota
AI Insights and AI Topics only cover 2 projects on Pro; the features the sales page leads with are effectively Business-plan features
Sentiment analysis still trips on sarcasm, mixed posts and non-English slang, so every client report needs a manual pass before you ship it
It is listening only - no publishing, inbox or engagement tools, so you still need a scheduler and a community inbox alongside it

faq.question: Is Brand24 worth it after the price increases?
faq.answer: Depends on what you attach to it. As a self-serve dashboard for one small brand, $199-249/mo is hard to defend when Google Alerts plus a Mention freebie covers 60% of the job. As the data layer for a sold service - monthly listening reports at $300-1,500 per client - the math flips fast: a Business plan at $599/mo annual can carry 5-8 client projects within its 25-keyword and 100K-mention caps. The tool is overpriced for hobbyists and underpriced for agencies.

faq.question: Does Brand24 have a free plan?
faq.answer: No permanent free tier - there is a 14-day trial on every plan, no card required to start. That trial is long enough to set up real keyword projects, measure your monthly mention volume and confirm the caps will not bite before you pay. Do that sizing exercise first: buying Individual for a brand that pulls 8,000 mentions a month is wasted money because you will be forced into Team within weeks.

faq.question: How accurate is Brand24's sentiment analysis?
faq.answer: Good enough for trends, not good enough to ship unreviewed. Straightforward praise and complaints classify reliably; sarcasm, irony, mixed-sentiment posts and non-English slang are where it stumbles. In practice you treat the sentiment chart as a directional signal and manually spot-check the flagged-negative mentions before anything reaches a client. The AI Insights summaries (Pro and up) help here - they cluster the conversation so you can check a handful of clusters instead of hundreds of posts.

faq.question: Brand24 vs Brandwatch - which should a small agency buy?
faq.answer: Brand24, unless a client contract explicitly demands Brandwatch's archive or compliance story. Brandwatch runs ~$800-5,000+/mo with quote-only pricing and an implementation fee; Brand24's top tier is $699/mo with a public price tag and a 14-day trial. Brandwatch holds a deeper historical archive (conversations back to 2008) and more advanced boolean work. For monitoring live mentions, alerting on spikes and producing monthly client reports, Brand24 covers 90% of the workflow at a fraction of the cost.

features: Mention tracking across 25M+ sources - social networks, news, blogs, forums, reviews, podcasts, video and newsletters in one feed
AI sentiment analysis on every mention, with manual re-tagging for the posts it misreads
Anomaly detection and instant alerts - email, Slack and app push when mention volume spikes against your baseline
AI Brand Assistant - ask questions about your mention data in plain English instead of building queries
AI Insights and AI Topics (Pro+) - auto-summarized conversation clusters and emerging themes per project
Presence Score, reach estimates, influencer identification and share-of-voice comparison against competitor projects
platform: Web app at app.brand24.com; iOS and Android apps for on-the-go monitoring; alerts via email, in-app and Slack; data export to CSV and PDF reports.
content:
Brand24 occupies the middle of the social-listening market that most guides skip over: serious source coverage without an enterprise sales call. It watches 25M+ sources - the big social networks plus TikTok, Twitch, Telegram, news sites, blogs, forums, review platforms and podcasts - pulls everything into one mention stream, and layers AI sentiment, anomaly alerts and (on higher plans) conversation summaries on top. For a solo consultant or small agency, that is the difference between catching a PR fire on Tuesday morning and reading about it in the client's email on Wednesday.

Honest framing first: this category has two poles. At one end, free Google Alerts that miss half the web; at the other, Brandwatch and Sprinklr at $2,000-5,000+/mo with onboarding fees and quote-only pricing. Brand24 lives between them, and after its recent price rises it sits closer to the expensive end than its marketing suggests. Whether it earns its seat depends almost entirely on what you sell around it.

## Pricing, Plainly

| Plan | Monthly | Annual (per mo) | Keywords | Mentions/mo | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Individual | $249 | $199 | 3 | 2K | 1 user, 12h updates |
| Team | $349 | $299 | 7 | 10K | Unlimited users, hourly updates |
| Pro | $499 | $399 | 12 | 40K | Realtime, AI Insights + Topics (2 projects) |
| Business | $699 | $599 | 25 | 100K | AI Insights (5 projects), Advanced Reports |
| Enterprise | quote | from $1,499 | Custom | Custom | AI Visibility module, dedicated consulting |

No free plan - a 14-day trial on every tier, no card to start. Annual billing knocks $50-100/mo off each tier.

Two things the pricing page will not volunteer. First, the hikes: reviews from 2025 list Individual at $79-149/mo. It is now $249 monthly. Whatever you sign up for, expect renewal-time sticker shock and take annual pricing while it lasts. Second, the AI features that headline the sales page - AI Insights, AI Topics - cover only 2 projects on Pro and 5 on Business. If your whole pitch to clients is the AI summaries, you are buying Business.

## The Money Angle: Sell the Monitoring, Not the Seat

Brand24 has an affiliate program, but the commission is pocket change next to the service margin. The real play is that one Business seat carries multiple client projects, and clients do not want a dashboard - they want a monthly answer to "what is the internet saying about us."

- **Monthly listening retainers.** Set up a project per client (brand name, founder, product lines, competitor keywords), then ship a 4-6 page monthly report: volume trend, sentiment split, top themes, notable posts, one recommendation. Agencies charge $300-1,500/mo per client for this. A Business plan at $599/mo annual with 25 keywords and 100K mentions comfortably serves 5-8 clients - the tool cost is $75-120 per client, the invoice is $500+.
- **Launch and campaign sprints.** Two to four weeks of daily monitoring around a product launch, funding announcement or rebrand. Charge $500-2,000 per sprint. The anomaly alerts do the watching; you do the judgment calls and the end-of-sprint readout.
- **Crisis-watch retainers.** The unglamorous but stickiest revenue: standing alert coverage with a response SLA. Small brands will pay $200-500/mo simply to know that if mentions triple at 2 a.m., a human (you) looks at it within the hour.
- **Competitor insight one-offs.** Pull a competitor project for two weeks and write up their sentiment weak spots, complaint themes and most-shared content. Charge $500-1,500 as a standalone audit - and it usually converts into the retainer above.

The tool's limits shape your pricing: keyword caps mean each client project needs careful query design (worth doing anyway - sloppy keywords are why most listening reports are garbage), and the sentiment pass needs your manual review, which is precisely the labor you are billing for.

## What It Actually Does Well

Source breadth is the honest selling point. Mention streams include places Google Alerts never touches - Twitch chats, Telegram channels, podcast transcripts, newsletter archives - and for niche consumer brands that is where the real conversations happen. Coverage on Instagram and Facebook comments is decent (via public data and API access), though private groups are off-limits like every competitor.

The alerting layer is the part worth paying for. Anomaly detection compares current volume against your project baseline and fires when something is off, into email, Slack or push. In crisis scenarios the value of the entire year's subscription is that one Tuesday-morning notification.

On Pro and up, AI Insights and AI Topics genuinely reduce report time - they cluster thousands of mentions into a handful of themes with summaries, so your monthly deliverable starts from a checked draft instead of a blank page. The AI Brand Assistant answers plain-English questions about your own data ("what drove the negative spike last week") with varying reliability; treat it as a starting point, not an analyst.

## Where It Falls Over

**The caps bite in real client work.** Three keywords on Individual is a joke for anything but a single-brand solo project - a brand, its misspelling and the founder's name exhaust it. Mention caps matter too: a consumer brand with 15K organic mentions/month blows through Team's 10K cap, and you will not discover this until the overage conversation. Size the plan against real mention volume during the trial before you commit.

**Sentiment needs human review.** Sarcasm and mixed posts get mislabeled at a rate that shows in any chart you ship unreviewed. Budget the QA pass into your retainer hours - and bill for it, because it is real work.

**No engagement, no publishing.** Brand24 listens and reports; it does not reply, schedule or hold an inbox. Agencies pair it with a scheduler and treat that as fine, but know it before buying.

**History is shallow next to Brandwatch.** You get trend data from your project start, not a decade-deep conversation archive. If a client's brief says "how has sentiment moved since 2022," Brand24 cannot answer from its own data.

## Who Should Skip It

If you are monitoring exactly one small brand with modest volume, Google Alerts plus manual checks may genuinely cover you. If you need deep historical archives, bespoke boolean research or regulated-industry compliance, that is Brandwatch territory - see our [Brandwatch breakdown](/tools/brandwatch/) for that end of the market. And if you have not yet, read our full [2026 social-listening comparison](/articles/best-ai-social-listening-tools-2026-brand24-vs-mention-vs-youscan-vs-brandwatch/) before deciding - Mention and YouScan both undercut Brand24 at the low end.

For everyone selling listening as a service, it is currently the strongest price-to-coverage ratio in the mid-market, hikes notwithstanding. Pair it with [GummySearch](/tools/gummysearch/) for Reddit-specific audience digging and [Ahrefs](/tools/ahrefs/) if the retainer extends into search visibility - they solve adjacent problems without overlapping Brand24's mention stream.

### Is the 14-day trial enough to evaluate it?

Yes, if you use it properly: build your real keyword projects, let them run the full 14 days, and check actual mention volume against plan caps on day 12. That single number - real monthly mentions per project - determines which plan you can sell against. Do not evaluate features; evaluate capacity.

### Can I resell Brand24 access directly to clients?

Not cleanly. There is no white-label mode, so client-facing value is your reports, not your login. The practical setup: run client projects inside your agency account, export the data and PDF reports, and deliver branded summaries. Clients pay for interpretation, and keeping them out of the raw dashboard is also what stops them from comparing your $500 report to the $199 tool under it.
